title: India Overhauls OCI Rules With Digital-First System and Stricter Compliance
excerpt: The Ministry of Home Affairs has introduced electronic OCI cards, dropped the six-month residency requirement for applicants, and imposed fines for late passport updates under the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026.
body:
India's Ministry of Home Affairs has overhauled the Overseas Citizen of India program for the first time in over a decade, introducing a fully digital registration system, broader eligibility criteria, and new compliance obligations that affect millions of diaspora members worldwide. The Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026, notified on April 30 and effective immediately, replace the paper-based OCI framework with an electronic platform centered on the portal ociservices.gov.in.

The changes also introduce the electronic OCI, or e-OCI, which launched on May 1. New applicants can now receive either a physical card or a digital registration recorded in the government's centralized electronic register. Existing physical cards remain valid, but all future services — fresh registration, passport updates, re-issuance, and renunciation — must be filed online.

  • India has launched e-OCI, a fully digital OCI card, and moved all applications to the online portal ociservices.gov.in, ending paper-based processing.
  • The six-month continuous stay requirement for applying within India has been dropped, and fifth- and sixth-generation Indian-origin Sri Lankan Tamils are now eligible for OCI status.
  • OCI holders who fail to update passport details on the portal within 90 days of receiving a new passport face a USD 25 fine.
  • Biometric consent for India's Fast Track Immigration Programme is now mandatory at OCI registration, with no option to opt out.

What Changed and Why

The Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026, published in the official gazette on April 30, amend the Citizenship Rules, 2009. All OCI applications under Section 7A of the Citizenship Act, 1955, must now be filed electronically in Form XXVIII through the designated portal. The earlier requirement of submitting documents in duplicate has been eliminated.

The MHA also removed the six-month continuous stay requirement for foreign nationals applying for OCI from within India. Applicants with a valid long-term visa and required documents can now submit their application soon after arrival, according to immigration consultancy Fragomen.

In a significant expansion, fifth- and sixth-generation Indian-origin Tamils in Sri Lanka can now apply for OCI cards — previously limited to the fourth generation. According to Fragomen, the change opens the program to "a broader group of Sri Lankan diaspora, particularly those from communities with limited historical documentation."

New Compliance Requirements

The overhaul introduces stricter compliance alongside expanded access. OCI holders must update their passport details on the portal within 90 days of receiving a new passport. The update is free within that window, but missing the deadline triggers a USD 25 fine. According to Wego, some travelers have already been asked to show proof of the update at Delhi and Bengaluru immigration counters.

The revised application form includes a mandatory biometric consent clause. Applicants must agree to share biometric information for India's Fast Track Immigration Programme, which enables automated e-gate processing at major airports. According to legal analysis by RPV Legal published on Mondaq, "there is no option to withhold consent entirely — in effect, linking biometric data to the Fast Track Immigration Programme is a condition of OCI registration."

"The amendments effect a transition from a paper-based and officer-driven administrative regime to a centralized digital system."

— RPV Legal, analysis published on Mondaq

The rules also tighten cancellation provisions. OCI registration may be cancelled if a holder is sentenced to two or more years in prison, or is charge-sheeted in a case carrying a potential punishment of seven years or more.

Impact on Diaspora Families

Fresh OCI registration now costs USD 275 for applicants outside India, following a fee revision effective April 1. A key clarification bars any minor from holding both an Indian passport and a foreign passport simultaneously. Parent-applicants must formally acknowledge this obligation on the application form, according to Livemint.

New appeal provisions allow rejections to be challenged before an authority one rank higher than the decision-maker. Applicants now have an express right to be heard before a final decision — a protection previously implied but not codified in the rules.

What's Next

The MHA expects processing times to drop to under 15 working days once legacy files migrate. The e-OCI will integrate with India's IVFRT 2.0 platform, the same system powering automated e-gates at major airports. Biometric data collected under the new consent requirement will support real-time passport and OCI data matching at these gates.

Existing physical OCI cardholders do not need to convert immediately. However, any future interaction with OCI services will route through the digital portal. Diaspora associations are expected to disseminate information about the new requirements, and the MHA is likely to issue detailed FAQs on the portal to assist applicants navigating the transition.
image_caption: India has launched a fully digital OCI registration system, replacing paper-based processing with the e-OCI platform
nri_angle: The overhaul directly impacts millions of OCI cardholders worldwide who must now navigate a digital-only portal, face fines for late passport updates, and consent to biometric data collection as part of India's modernized immigration framework.
author: Diaspora Desk
